Plot Runs of Homozygosity

plot_roh.Rd

Generate a plot displaying the locations of ROHs across the genome. Takes either a snpRdata object for which ROH information has been calculated or a data.frame with ROH info.

Usage

plot_roh(x, facet = NULL, chr = "chr", bp = "position", lab_as_other = NULL)

Arguments

x

snpRdata object or an object coercible to a data.frame. If a snpRdata object, needs to have had ROH info calculated with calc_roh. If present in the sample metadata or in the provided data.table, the column "sampID" will be taken as sample IDs for plotting. data.frames should have columns:

  • start_position: start positions for ROHs

  • end_position: end positions for ROHs

  • sampID: sample IDs

  • chr_len: total chromosome lengths for the chromosomes on which ROHs were detected.

  • chr: a column containing chromosome info named to match the chr argument! Note that for data.frame inputs, chromosomes or individuals with no ROHs will not be plotted.

facet

character. sample facet by which to color individuals. Note that only one facet is plotable at a time.

chr

character, default "chr". Column in either snp metadata or x (for snpRdata or data.frame objects, respectively) which defines the "chromosome" by which SNP positions will be concatenated along the x-axis.

bp

character, default "bp". Column in either snp metadata which defines the position in bp of each SNP. Ignored for data.table inputs.

lab_as_other

character vector, default NULL. Vector of chromosome/scaffold names which will be plotted grouped together, labelled as "other". Useful for small scaffolds/etc.

Value

A ggplot2 plot showing the positions of ROHs (white areas) against colored chromosomal backdrops. Note that the data used to plot this can be returned by calling $data on the resulting object.
